questions.prompt: Which service issues the access tokens (JWTs) that a client uses to call APIs?
options: The Identity Provider, because it stores the passwords
The resource API itself, on every request
The Authorization Server, which handles OAuth 2.0/OIDC, defines scopes and grants permissions
questions.explanation: The IdP answers "Who are you?" and is the source of truth for credentials; the Authorization Server answers "What are you allowed to do?" and issues the tokens.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of an Identity Provider and Authorization Server working together in order.
steps: The user's login request goes to the Authorization Server
The Authorization Server asks the Identity Provider whether the user is who they say they are
The Identity Provider checks its database and confirms the user
The Authorization Server decides what the user may do and issues a signed JWT
The client presents the JWT to the API, which trusts the Authorization Server's signature
questions.explanation: The IdP verifies identity; the Authorization Server turns that into a signed token carrying permissions, which the API trusts because of the signature.

questions.prompt: What does OpenID Connect add on top of OAuth 2.0?
options: An authentication layer: the ID token and the UserInfo endpoint
questions.explanation: OAuth 2.0 covers authorization (access and refresh tokens, scopes, client credentials); OIDC builds on it with ID tokens, UserInfo and authentication.

source.section: How Auth Server, OpenIddict, OAuth 2.0, and OpenID Connect (OIDC) relate to each other

questions.prompt: How does the lesson describe the relationship between an Identity Provider and an authentication server?
options: An Identity Provider is one small part of an authentication server
An authentication server is typically one component of an Identity Provider, which also covers user management, MFA, password reset and registration
An Identity Provider only works with OAuth 2.0, never with OIDC
questions.explanation: An IdP is a trusted system that manages identities and authenticates users; it often includes an authentication server along with OAuth 2.0 and OIDC support.
